answer: Resist sybils by making parallelism expensive. Before an identity can affect settlement, the kernel requires a locked deposit plus a one-at-a-time delay: each new key from the same funding cluster adds a longer freeze, queued against a marble wall of prior locks. Weight toward a zenith accrues only as those deposits age without a slash for correlated signing. Cloning ten accounts means ten frozen balances and ten staggered waits, so flooding a vote costs more capital-time than the vote can pay.
